intervals.note: Spans CERN LEPC approval to OPAL's own quoted stop date. Operating interval; the terminal event is its end.

intervals.note: Spans CERN LEPC approval to OPAL's own quoted stop date. Terminal event: the end of the operating interval above.

country_count.note: Eight countries named: Canada, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Israel, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States. The source gives no date for this figure; as_of (2026-09) is when it was read, not when it was true.

institution_count.note: '34 institutes' per OPAL's own welcome page. The source gives no date for this figure; as_of (2026-09) is when it was read, not when it was true.
institution_count.quote: Currently the collaboration consists of about 200 physicists from 34 institutes in Canada, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Israel, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States.

member_count.note: 'about 200 physicists' per the same source; described as approximate. The source gives no date for this figure; as_of (2026-09) is when it was read, not when it was true.

summary.plain: The international team of about 200 physicists from 34 institutes who built and ran the OPAL detector at CERN's LEP collider.
summary.technical: Approved by the CERN LEPC on 18 November 1982; about 200 physicists from 34 institutes in Canada, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Israel, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States (OPAL's own welcome page).
